items.title: 63477_Joe Darensbourg oral history interview
items.q: I can't really pinpoint, except one of the highlights was Raphael Mendez... old Raphael Mendez brought his trumpet up there

ctx.x: No one has ever sort of brought that out about Ory's band. The George Lewis band, which was going around the same time, you often see tapes of them at parties with different musicians, and playing with young guys, different players -- Johnny Williams sometimes would come play trumpet at a jam session. But Ory... I've very seldom heard any tapes or recordings of anything. So you were corroborating that it was a band mostly, then, that sort of stayed to itself, and played professionally when it was working, and…

No. We didn't go out together anyway. I always really went my way. I remember one time, though... Once in a while, musicians, a famous musician would come up to Beverly Cavern, where we played, and the owner would let them sit in. I can't really pinpoint, except one of the highlights was Raphael Mendez. I don't know if you know who he is...

items.title: 63477_Joe Darensbourg oral history interview
items.q: He said, 'Rafe is crazy about this kind of music, and he'd like to try to play some of it.' ... old Raphael Mendez brought his trumpet up there

ctx.x: said, "Hey, do you think..." He said, "Rafe is crazy about this kind of music, and he'd like to try to play some of it." And he said, "Do you think Kid Ory would let him sit in and try?" I said, "I think he would." Because Ory admired him, too. Because the guy was really an artist. And I think he used to let guys sit in on a Monday night if they wanted to -- if they could play. And old Raphael Mendez brought his trumpet up there, I'll never forget it. He wanted to play "Basin Street Blues" the first thing!…
Strangely enough, I was in New Orleans one time, and you know this boy who's got the Tijuana Brass, Herb Alpert or whatever his name is...?
